variableValveTiming.note: English Wikipedia's Supra article says both Japanese engines got VVT-i in 1997; Japanese Wikipedia says the NA engine did not, and every Toyota and catalogue spec page shows the NA rating and 10.0:1 compression unchanged to 2002 (VVT-i 2JZ-GEs elsewhere run 10.5:1). compressionRatio.note: Sources disagree. Toyota's 1998 Supra Product Source prints 10.0:1 for the 1998 non-turbo. Lexus's own 1998 GS specification sheet gives 10.5:1 for the GS 300's VVT-i 2JZ-GE, which carries the identical 225 hp @ 6,000 / 220 lb-ft @ 4,000 rating, and engine-specs.net gives 10.5:1 for VVT-i 2JZ-GEs in general. 10.5 is kept because the Product Source row looks carried over from the pre-VVT-i engine (10.0:1), but it stays single-source until a 1998 Supra repair manual or New Car Features page settles it.

variants.notes: Exists only in the US: Toyota USA adds VVT-i to the 1998 non-turbo, while the Japanese Supra's 2JZ-GE never got it. Toyota's 1998 Product Source confirms the 1998 non-turbo (models 2396 and 2394) and makes the 4-speed ECT-i automatic its only gearbox (the 5-speed models were deleted). English Wikipedia's claim that the NA engine was dropped in the US for 1998 is therefore wrong. The 1998 Turbo was not sold in California-emissions states.
